description: Chat completions end to end: the OpenAI-compatible front (horde-oai) traffic, latency, capacity and wake sources from app OTLP metrics on mimir-telemetry; the horde's native chat routes and chat return codes; the front's finished-request log line on loki-app; and chat traces in Tempo.

panels.title: Front traffic (OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions)

panels.description: Chat requests that took an in-flight slot over the dashboard range. Source: horde.oai.requests.admitted.
panels.title: Admitted

panels.description: Completions delivered to the client over the range. Source: horde.oai.completions.
panels.title: Completions delivered

panels.description: Completions divided by admitted requests over the range. Client disconnects, timeouts, horde refusals and faults all lower it.
panels.title: Delivered share of admitted

panels.description: Requests refused before taking an in-flight slot: body size or read timeout, validation, authorization, front at capacity.
panels.title: Refused before admission

panels.description: Admitted requests answered with an error status before any header: horde refusals at submit, timeouts, no eligible worker, faults, horde unavailable.
panels.title: Errors after admission

panels.description: Streamed requests whose 200 headers were sent and which then ended in an SSE error event.
panels.title: Stream failures after headers

panels.description: Admitted requests by streamed flag, and completions delivered.
panels.title: Admitted and delivered per minute

panels.description: Completions by the model a worker served. 'usage estimated' counts completions whose token usage the front estimated because the worker did not report it.
panels.title: Delivered completions per minute, by model

panels.description: Cancels the front sent to the horde, by outcome, and requests carrying an SDK retry count above zero (clients retrying after an error).
panels.title: Cancels and client retries per minute

panels.description: Refusals before an in-flight slot. FrontAtCapacity (503) means the front's global or per-source cap was reached.
panels.title: Refused before admission per minute, by status and code

panels.description: Admitted requests that ended in an error status before any header. '(none)' is a status without a code, such as a 429 passed through from the horde.
panels.title: Errors after admission per minute, by status and code

panels.description: Streams that ended in an SSE error event after 200 headers.
panels.title: Stream failures per minute, by code

panels.description: Every admitted request by final code, HTTP status and streamed flag. A stream records status 200 whatever its outcome; 'ok' is a delivered completion and 'client_closed' a client that disconnected first.
panels.title: Request outcomes over the range

panels.description: Requests refused before an in-flight slot, by code and status.
panels.title: Refusals before admission over the range
Front latency

panels.description: From an admitted request's arrival to its end, including the wait for a worker. A streamed request lasts until its stream ends.
panels.title: Request duration p50 / p95, by streamed and status

panels.description: From the submit acknowledgement to the first content sent: the first completion chunk, or the non-streamed body.
panels.title: Time to first content p50 / p95, by streamed

panels.description: The horde's queue_wait_seconds of each delivered generation: request creation to assignment to a worker.
panels.title: Queue wait p50 / p95, by model

panels.description: Latency of each call from the front to the horde's native API, from taking a call slot to the answer. 'refused' is a horde status of 400 or above; 'abandoned' means the request's budget ended first.
panels.title: Native call duration p95, by call type and outcome

panels.description: Calls from the front to the horde's native API. Status reads dominate while requests wait.
panels.title: Native calls per second, by call type and outcome

panels.description: Size of each request body received whole. Oversized bodies are counted as refusals instead.
panels.title: Request body size p50 / p95

panels.description: Server-side duration from the front's HTTP instrumentation (milliseconds). Requests to unknown paths carry no route.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_method, http_target, http_status_code) (rate(http_server_duration_bucket{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment"}[5m])))

panels.title: Front HTTP p95, by route and status

panels.description: Client-side duration of the front's HTTP calls to the horde (milliseconds), from the HTTP client instrumentation.
panels.title: Front calls to the horde p95, by method and status
Front capacity

panels.description: Requests holding an in-flight slot. The dashed line is the front's default global cap (100); a deployment can set another.
panels.title: Requests holding an in-flight slot

panels.description: Distinct client addresses holding at least one slot, and the most slots one address holds. The dashed line is the default per-source cap (5); a deployment can set another.

targets.legendFormat: slots held by the busiest address

panels.title: Distinct sources and the busiest source

panels.description: Requests the front's HTTP server is handling, including streams still open.
panels.title: Active HTTP requests in the front server, by method

panels.description: All responses of the front's HTTP server.
panels.title: Front HTTP responses per second, by route and status

panels.description: The front's HTTP calls to the horde: POST submits, GET status reads and models, DELETE cancels.
panels.title: Front calls to the horde per second, by method and status
Wake sources (how waiting requests learn they finished)

panels.description: Each status read of a waiting request by its cause: immediate (after the submit), signal, recheck, poll, deadline; and disconnect, recorded without a read.
panels.title: Status reads per minute, by wake source

panels.description: Of the status reads that found the request finished, the share per wake source. A high poll share means the completion signal is not reaching the front.

targets.expr: sum by (horde_wake_source) (rate(horde_oai_wakes{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_found_finished="true"}[5m])) / ignoring (horde_wake_source) group_left sum(rate(horde_oai_wakes{job="ai-horde/horde-oai", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_found_finished="true"}[5m]))

panels.title: Share of finishes found, by wake source

panels.description: Share of finished requests found through the completion signal over the range.
panels.title: Finishes found by signal
Horde native chat API (/api/v2/generate/chat)

panels.description: Requests to the horde's native chat routes, from every client including the front.
panels.title: Chat route requests per second, by route and status

panels.description: Server-side duration of the native chat routes (milliseconds).
panels.title: Chat route latency p50 / p95, by route

panels.description: Share of chat route responses with a 5xx status. Absent when there were none.

targets.expr: sum by (http_target) (rate(http_server_duration_count{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_target=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*", http_status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (http_target) (rate(http_server_duration_count{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_target=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*"}[5m])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Chat route 5xx share, by route

panels.description: Refusals on the chat routes, plus chat return codes on any route (for example a worker's chat reply refused at text submit).

targets.expr: sum by (horde_rc, http_route, http_response_status_code) (increase(horde_api_rejections{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", http_route=~"/api/v2/generate/chat/.*"}[$__range])) or sum by (horde_rc, http_route, http_response_status_code) (increase(horde_api_rejections{job="ai-horde/ai-horde", deployment_environment_name=~"$environment", horde_rc=~".*Chat.*"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Chat refusals by return code over the range

panels.description: Chat replies the horde refused when a worker submitted them: ChatSubmitInvalid (no client could use it) and ChatSubmitNonconformant (broke a strict request's tool_choice or response_format). Per-worker counts are on the text worker dashboards.
panels.title: Worker chat replies refused at submit, per minute
Finished-request log (front)

panels.description: One 'Chat request ... finished:' line per admitted request, parsed. woke_by is the wake source of the read that found the request finished; None for a timeout, fail-fast or horde error. Filter with $code and $host.

targets.expr: sum by (code, woke_by, streamed) (count_over_time({app="ai-horde", component="oai", instance=~"$host"} |= "finished: streamed=" | regexp "streamed=(?P<streamed>\\S+) .* woke_by=(?P<woke_by>\\S+) .* code=(?P<code>\\S+)" | code=~"$code" [$__range]))

panels.title: Finished requests by code, wake source and streamed

panels.description: The front's finished-request line. Use the Code variable to pick outcomes; the line carries no key, prompt, title or client address.
panels.title: Finished-request lines

panels.description: Lines the horde writes for chat refusals (the return code, then the reason; this includes worker replies refused at submit) and chat warnings such as failed image or fault-reason storage.
panels.title: Horde chat refusals and warnings
Traces

panels.description: Root spans of chat requests at the front, newest first. Open a trace to see the horde's spans beneath. Trace retention is short; keep ranges within a day.
panels.title: Recent chat requests

panels.description: Chat requests that took over 30 seconds or ended with an error status.
panels.title: Slow or failed chat requests
